key_insight: Z-GRO avoids large constraint penalties by combining feasibility-protecting quantum evolution with closed-loop spectral cooling to favor feasible, low-cost solutions.
engineering_relevance: The scheme targets constrained binary optimization on dynamic quantum circuits while reducing penalty-related spectral aliasing and two-qubit gate overhead.
method: Embed reversible feasibility phase operators in symmetric dynamical-decoupling echoes to protect the feasible subspace.
Use an interaction-correlated commutator gauge to overcome initial symmetry stall and ancilla-assisted cooling to favor lower objective values.
Advance a cooling threshold from a linear-programming bound using survival-filtered Ramsey feedback and automatic overshoot rollback.
evidence_signal: Density-matrix and trajectory simulations on spin-glass and quadratic knapsack ensembles report 3.0–4.3× higher ground-state probability than quantum Zeno dynamics and 2.4–14.5× lower time-to-solution for 14-qubit knapsack instances.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; hardware performance remains to be validated under realistic feedback latency and feasibility-oracle implementation costs.
paper_title: Penalty-Free Constrained Optimization on Dynamic Quantum Circuits via Phase-Protected Tunneling and Closed-Loop Spectral Ratchets
